steps.subject: Revert "[SelectionDAG] Expand CTTZ_ELTS[_ZERO_POISON] and handle splitting" (#188220)

evidence: Reverts a risky SelectionDAG legalization change that had caused ISel crashes, so it is a plausible regression boundary candidate
Even so, the reverted feature is cttz.elts handling, not the X86 bit-test/low-bits mechanism named in the issue
features: ISel crash history, SelectionDAG legalization, meta:core-llvm, meta:revert, path:llvm/include/llvm/CodeGen, path:llvm/lib/CodeGen/SelectionDAG
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This revert removes the CTTZ_ELTS/CTTZ_ELTS_ZERO_POISON legalization and expansion support that had been added previously. It deletes the dedicated TargetLowering::expandCttzElts helper and backs out the SelectionDAGBuilder, vector legalization, and integer/vector type-legalization hooks for these opcodes, restoring the prior behavior where those nodes are not specially handled by the reverted code.
Changed symbols: DAGTypeLegalizer::SplitVectorOperand; DAGTypeLegalizer::PromoteIntegerOperand; TargetLowering::expandCttzElts; SelectionDAGBuilder::visitIntrinsicCall; VectorLegalizer::LegalizeOp; VectorLegalizer::Expand
Behavioral change: Removes explicit legalization/expansion support for CTTZ_ELTS and CTTZ_ELTS_ZERO_POISON.; Restores the earlier intrinsic lowering path that conditionally expanded the operation in SelectionDAGBuilder.; Eliminates the dedicated generic expansion algorithm that computed trailing-zero element counts via vector reduction.
Assertion or trace link: SelectionDAG; DAG combine; X86ISelLowering.cpp; low bits constraint must survive width adjustment; peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc; combineBTToBitOpFlag
Reproducer link: Clang crashes at -O1 during X86 DAG instruction selection; assertion failure in backend lowering
Pass or subsystem link: SelectionDAG; LegalizeVectorTypes; LegalizeIntegerTypes; SelectionDAGBuilder
Causal explanation: Because this is a revert of the prior SelectionDAG CTTZ_ELTS legalization work, it likely undoes a backend change that may have introduced regressions. However, the retrieved hunks still do not mention the X86 low-bits assertion or bit-test combine logic from the issue, so the link is indirect: it is a plausible rollback of a risky backend change, but not evidence of the specific crash mechanism.
Causal confidence: 0.31
Build risk: Reverts core SelectionDAG legalization behavior; Affects intrinsic lowering and vector legalization across targets; May change codegen for scalable and fixed-width vectors; High regression risk due to removal of previously added support

top_candidates.subject: [SelectionDAG] Remove `NoNaNsFPMath` uses (#183448)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This change removes SelectionDAG's dependence on the global NoNaNsFPMath target option when determining whether an operation is known never-NaN, leaving only per-node no-nans flags as evidence. The accompanying X86 test updates adjust expected floating-point minimum/maximum lowering patterns under no-nans and no-signed-zeros combinations.
Changed symbols: SelectionDAG::isKnownNeverNaN; llvm/test/CodeGen/X86/fminimum-fmaximum.ll; llvm/test/CodeGen/X86/fminimumnum-fmaximumnum.ll; llvm/test/CodeGen/X86/avx512fp16-fminimum-fmaximum.ll
Behavioral change: Stops treating the target-wide NoNaNsFPMath option as sufficient to prove a value is never NaN.; Narrows NaN reasoning to explicit IR/node flags only.; Adjusts X86 floating-point min/max codegen expectations accordingly.
Assertion or trace link: low bits constraint must survive width adjustment; peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc; combineBTToBitOpFlag
Reproducer link: Clang crashes at -O1 during X86 DAG instruction selection
Pass or subsystem link: SelectionDAG; X86 floating-point combine/codegen
Causal explanation: The hunks are entirely about floating-point NaN inference and X86 min/max tests, with no visible interaction with bit-test lowering, integer width adjustment, or the named assertion. Based on the retrieved context, this commit is unlikely to be the direct cause of the reported X86 DAG combine crash.
Causal confidence: 0.08
Build risk: Backend analysis change in SelectionDAG; Affects codegen decisions across targets; Test updates indicate observable lowering changes

Summary: This change extends SelectionDAG unsigned-division-by-constant lowering to optionally widen 32-bit scalar divisions on 64-bit targets when wide 64-bit multiply/high-multiply support is available. It threads new AllowWiden and UseWiden decisions through BuildUDIV, changes the magic-constant materialization to use a 64-bit constant when widening is selected, and adds a new lowering path that zero-extends the dividend, performs a 64x64->128 multiply via MULHU or UMUL_LOHI, then truncates the high half back to the original type. The commit also adds X86 tests covering the new widened constant-division codegen.

selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit renames and refactors SelectionDAG's constant-identity helper from a global neutral-constant predicate into SelectionDAG methods that can account for demanded vector elements. The DAG combiner and vector legalization sites are updated to call SelectionDAG::isIdentityElement, and the implementation now threads demanded-elements information into floating-point constant handling. The visible change is confined to SelectionDAG combine/legalization logic and does not touch X86 lowering directly.
Changed symbols: DAGCombiner::foldSelectWithIdentityConstant; SelectionDAG::getNeutralElement; SelectionDAG::getIdentityElement; SelectionDAG::isIdentityElement; DAGTypeLegalizer::WidenVecOp_VECREDUCE; llvm::isNeutralConstant
Behavioral change: Identity-element checks now use SelectionDAG methods instead of the old free function.; The check can consider demanded vector elements when classifying floating-point constants.; Vector reduce widening and select folding now rely on the new identity-element API.
Assertion or trace link: low bits constraint must survive width adjustment; peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc; combineBTToBitOpFlag; X86ISelLowering.cpp
Reproducer link: Clang crashes at -O1 during X86 DAG instruction selection; backend assertion during SelectionDAG combine
Pass or subsystem link: SelectionDAG combine; SelectionDAG legalization; DAGCombiner
Causal explanation: The issue is about an X86 DAG-combine assertion involving low-bit constraints and bit-test lowering. This commit only changes generic SelectionDAG identity-element reasoning and vector reduction/select folding; the retrieved hunks do not show any X86-specific bit-test, truncation, or width-adjustment logic. It is therefore only weakly related as a generic DAG-combine change, with no direct evidence that it addresses or triggers the reported assertion.
Causal confidence: 0.18
Build risk: Touches core SelectionDAG combine/utility APIs used broadly by codegen; Changes constant-folding behavior for vector and floating-point identities; Potentially affects many targets through generic DAGCombiner and legalization paths

top_candidates.subject: [SelectionDAG] Use Magic Algorithm for Splitting UDIV/UREM by Constant (#154968)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit refactors and expands constant division/remainder expansion in TargetLowering by introducing new helpers for unsigned division/remainder via magic-number decomposition and multiplication-based lowering. The retrieved hunks show substantial algorithmic work in SelectionDAG TargetLowering, plus new X86 tests for divide-by-constant and divmod128 cases that exercise preshift/postshift and large-constant handling.
Changed symbols: TargetLowering::expandUDIVREMByConstantViaUREMDecomposition; TargetLowering::expandUDIVREMByConstantViaUMulHiMagic; TargetLowering::expandDIVREMByConstant; MakeMUL_LOHIByConst; MakeAddSubLong; MakeSRLLong; divide-by-constant.ll; divmod128.ll
Behavioral change: Splits unsigned div/rem-by-constant lowering into dedicated decomposition and magic-multiply paths.; Uses known leading zeros to choose a potentially smaller magic divisor algorithm.; Adds helpers to build long add/sub and shift operations across split scalar halves.; Changes constant division/remainder expansion behavior for preshift/postshift and large constants.
Assertion or trace link: SelectionDAG; TargetLowering; divide-by-constant; magic algorithm; preshift; postshift
Reproducer link: New tests cover constant div/rem lowering on X86 and divmod128; No direct crash or assertion text from the reported low-bits constraint issue appears in the retrieved hunks
Pass or subsystem link: SelectionDAG TargetLowering; X86 constant division/remainder lowering
Causal explanation: The commit is clearly backend-lowering heavy and touches integer-width reasoning, which is adjacent to the reported X86 DAG combine crash. Still, the retrieved hunks focus on constant division/remainder expansion rather than bit-test lowering or the specific low-bits constraint assertion, so the evidence for this exact issue is moderate at best.
Causal confidence: 0.41
Build risk: Large algorithmic change in TargetLowering constant div/rem expansion; Touches core SelectionDAG lowering helpers and new helper declarations; Adds extensive X86 codegen tests for multiple ABIs and widths

top_candidates.subject: [DAGCombiner] Teach `reduceLoadWidth` to look past `ISD:FREEZE` (#189317)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit teaches SelectionDAG's reduceLoadWidth combine to look through ISD::FREEZE when the freeze sits between an integer operation and a load, and adds a new X86 test file covering freeze-plus-load narrowing cases. The implementation also preserves semantics for multi-use freezes by bailing out in unsafe cases, replacing old load uses when appropriate, and rewrapping narrowed results with freeze and assert nodes.
Changed symbols: DAGCombiner::visitAND; DAGCombiner::reduceLoadWidth; FreezeNode; DAG.ReplaceAllUsesOfValueWith; ISD::FREEZE; ISD::AssertZext; ISD::AssertSext; reduce-load-width-freeze.ll
Behavioral change: Allows load-width reduction through a freeze node instead of stopping at freeze.; Bails out when a multi-use freeze would make narrowing unsafe, except for safe anyext-to-zext style changes.; Replaces all uses of the original load value for multi-use freezes so all consumers see the narrowed load.; Rewraps narrowed results in freeze and adds assert-zext/assert-sext nodes to preserve range information.
Assertion or trace link: SelectionDAG; DAGCombiner; reduceLoadWidth; freeze; assert
Reproducer link: New tests show masked/truncated loads through freeze lowering to narrower loads; Covers volatile and non-volatile freeze/load cases
Pass or subsystem link: SelectionDAG DAGCombiner; X86 codegen tests
Causal explanation: This is plausibly related to the reported X86 DAG combine crash because it directly changes integer width reasoning in SelectionDAG and explicitly handles freeze, assert-zext, and assert-sext around narrowed loads. However, the retrieved hunks do not mention the specific low-bits assertion or bit-test lowering helpers from the issue, so the link is indirect rather than exact.
Causal confidence: 0.74
Build risk: Core SelectionDAG combine logic changed; Touches load narrowing and value replacement semantics; Adds new X86 backend regression tests for freeze-related combines

The X86 vector overflow tests are updated to match the new lowering shape.
Changed symbols: TargetLowering::expandSADDSUBO; DAGTypeLegalizer::ExpandIntRes_SADDSUBO; llvm/test/CodeGen/X86/vec_ssubo.ll; llvm/test/CodeGen/X86/ssub_sat_vec.ll

Summary: This X86 lowering change adds a special-case lowering for vector i8 arithmetic right shift by 1, using an average-with-all-ones formulation plus masking to emulate signed shift semantics. Changed symbols: LowerShiftByScalarImmediate; X86ISelLowering; SelectionDAG; getFreeze

Assertion or trace link: low bits constraint must survive width adjustment; X86 DAG combine; SelectionDAG
Reproducer link: Clang crashes at -O1 during X86 DAG instruction selection; integer width/sign-extension reasoning in backend lowering

The evidence supports only a loose subsystem-level connection to the crash.

top_candidates.subject: [X86] LowerBUILD_VECTORvXi1 - attempt to fold as VPTESTMB(BUILD_VECTOR_vXi8(X),1) (#198166)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit extends X86 lowering for BUILD_VECTOR of vXi1 to attempt a cheaper lowering through vXi8 vectors, with a fallback to vXi32 on pre-BWI targets. The retrieved hunk adds a new lowering path that materializes a byte vector, zero-extends it, masks with 1, and compares against zero.
Changed symbols: LowerBUILD_VECTORvXi1; LowerBUILD_VECTORvXbf16; SelectionDAG; BUILD_VECTOR; ANY_EXTEND; AND; getSetCC
Behavioral change: Introduces a new lowering strategy for vector i1 build-vectors via byte vectors.; Selects a wider intermediate type depending on BWI support.; Adds a compare-against-zero formulation to produce the final vXi1 result.
Assertion or trace link: low bits constraint must survive width adjustment; peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc; combineBTToBitOpFlag; X86ISelLowering.cpp
Reproducer link: Clang crashes at -O1 during X86 DAG instruction selection
Pass or subsystem link: X86ISelLowering.cpp; SelectionDAG lowering
Causal explanation: This is a real X86 lowering change involving vector width adjustment and bit-level reasoning, which is in the same subsystem family as the reported assertion. Still, the retrieved code is about BUILD_VECTOR vXi1 lowering rather than bit-test combine or low-bits constraint preservation, so the connection to the exact crash is only moderate.
Causal confidence: 0.58
Build risk: Touches target lowering in X86ISelLowering.cpp; Adds a new legalization-sensitive lowering path; Depends on target feature checks and vector type legality

top_candidates.subject: [X86] combineVectorInsert - attempt to merge consecutive constant insertions (#198273)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This X86 lowering change extends combineVectorInsert to recognize adjacent constant element insertions and replace two scalar inserts with one wider vector insert plus bitcast. It also adds an out-of-range INSERT_VECTOR_ELT poison fold. The transformation is gated on legal integer vector types and uses APInt packing to merge the two constants into a wider scalar constant.
Changed symbols: combineVectorInsert; X86ISelLowering; SelectionDAG; TargetLowering; SDValue
Behavioral change: Adds a new combine that merges neighboring constant insertelement operations into a single wider insert_vector_elt/bitcast sequence.; Introduces a new poison result for constant INSERT_VECTOR_ELT indices that are out of range.; Changes vector-insert canonicalization to reason about element width and vector legality when packing constants.
Assertion or trace link: low bits constraint must survive width adjustment; X86 DAG combine; SelectionDAG; X86ISelLowering.cpp

This patch directly changes X86 SelectionDAG combine behavior in the same lowering file, but the visible logic is about vector insert folding rather than bit-test or low-bits constraint reasoning. top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes X86 GlobalISel lowering for chained unsigned add/sub carry handling. In selectUAddSub, it replaces a compare-against-1 materialization of the carry-in byte with a NEG8r on that byte, so the carry flag is derived directly from the byte value before the following ADC/SBB. The accompanying tests update expected codegen from CMP8ri to NEG8r for i64/i128 add/sub cases.
Changed symbols: X86InstructionSelector::selectUAddSub; MachineInstr; BuildMI; createVirtualRegister; NEG8r
Behavioral change: Carry-in materialization changes from byte compare to flag-setting negation.; The selector now treats the carry-in as a SETB-produced byte and converts it to EFLAGS.CF via NEG.; This alters instruction selection only in GlobalISel add/sub carry chains, not SelectionDAG lowering.

top_candidates.subject: [X86] Fold XOR of VGF2P8AFFINEQB and its source (#198448)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit adds and extends X86 GFNI xor-folding combines in X86ISelLowering.cpp, including a new fold for xor-ing a GF2P8AFFINEQB result with its source operand by rewriting the affine matrix with an identity contribution. It also updates X86 codegen tests to cover several constant-matrix, variable-matrix, and multi-use cases for the new combine.
Changed symbols: combineXorWithGF2P8AFFINEQB; X86::isConstantSplat; getTargetConstantBitsFromNode; X86ISD::GF2P8AFFINEQB; llvm/test/CodeGen/X86/gfni-xor-fold.ll; llvm/test/CodeGen/X86/gfni-xor-fold-avx512.ll; llvm/test/CodeGen/X86/gfni-operand-and-fold.ll
Behavioral change: Adds a new combine that recognizes GF2P8AFFINEQB(x, M) ^ x and folds it into a single GF2P8AFFINEQB with a transformed matrix; Introduces constant-bit extraction from the xor operand to build a new affine matrix; Preserves non-folding behavior for multi-use or variable-matrix cases via tests; Expands X86 DAG combine logic in a target-specific lowering file

Reproducer link: Clang crashes at -O1 during X86 DAG instruction selection; Issue involves backend combine logic and integer-width reasoning

top_candidates.subject: [SelectionDAG] Widen <2 x T> vector types for atomic store (#197618)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit adds SelectionDAG legalization support for widening atomic vector stores. It introduces coerceStoredValue and DAGTypeLegalizer::WidenVecOp_ATOMIC_STORE, wires ATOMIC_STORE into vector widening, and adds X86 tests for atomic stores of widened vector types. The change is in generic SelectionDAG vector legalization rather than X86-specific combine logic.
Changed symbols: coerceStoredValue; DAGTypeLegalizer::WidenVecOp_ATOMIC_STORE; DAGTypeLegalizer::WidenVectorOperand; LegalizeVectorTypes.h; atomic-load-store.ll
Behavioral change: Adds a legalization path that widens atomic vector stores by extracting/coercing the original value into a memory-width-compatible scalar/vector and emitting an atomic store of the widened type.; Uses findMemType with StAlign=0 to avoid widening past the original object when selecting the store width.; Extends vector widening handling to ATOMIC_STORE, which previously had no dedicated widening path.
Assertion or trace link: low bits constraint must survive width adjustment; SelectionDAG; width adjustment
Reproducer link: Clang crashes at -O1 during backend instruction selection
Pass or subsystem link: SelectionDAG LegalizeVectorTypes; atomic store legalization
Causal explanation: This commit is in SelectionDAG legalization, which is adjacent to the reported crash area, but the hunks are about atomic vector store widening rather than X86 bit-test lowering or low-bits constraint propagation. The added logic could influence width-adjustment behavior in general, yet the retrieved context does not show any interaction with peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc or combineBTToBitOpFlag. The link to the issue is therefore indirect and speculative.
Causal confidence: 0.22

Summary: This commit adds X86 DAG combine support to merge a BT with a matching bit-modifying operation into a single flag-producing BTR/BTS/BTC node. It introduces new X86ISD fragments and a combineBTToBitOpFlag helper that peeks through truncation, zero-extension, any-extension, and low-bit-preserving AND masks on bit positions before fusing the operations.
Changed symbols: X86bt; X86btr; X86bts; X86btc; peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc; combineBTToBitOpFlag; combineBT; llvm/test/CodeGen/X86/bt-merge-fuse.ll

top_candidates.subject: [X86] lowerShuffleWithPSHUFB - use getConstVector to create shuffle mask (#201122)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes X86 PSHUFB shuffle lowering to build the shuffle mask as a constant vector via getConstVector instead of a vector of SDValues built from constants/undefs. The hunk is confined to lowerShuffleWithPSHUFB and associated shuffle tests, adjusting how the mask is materialized in SelectionDAG.
Changed symbols: lowerShuffleWithPSHUFB; getConstVector; X86ISD::PSHUFB; shuffle_v64i8_to_v32i8; shuffle_v64i8_to_v32i8_1
Behavioral change: Represents PSHUFB masks as integer lane values rather than per-lane SDValue constants; Changes the DAG shape for shuffle-mask construction before emitting PSHUFB; Updates expected codegen from direct vpshufb mask materialization to broadcasted constant-vector forms in tests
Assertion or trace link: low bits constraint must survive width adjustment; peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc; combineBTToBitOpFlag
Reproducer link: Clang crashes at -O1 during X86 DAG instruction selection
Pass or subsystem link: X86ISelLowering; SelectionDAG combine; shuffle lowering
Causal explanation: This is an X86 lowering change, but it targets PSHUFB shuffle-mask construction rather than bit-test combines or low-bit width adjustment. The issue signature is specifically about BT/bit-op flag combining and an assertion in bit-position peeling, so the connection is weak and only indirect through general DAG-shape changes.
Causal confidence: 0.28
Build risk: Touches X86ISelLowering; SelectionDAG DAG-shape change; Test-only updates for shuffle codegen

top_candidates.subject: [X86] Move Non-VLX handling for VPMADD52 instructions entirely into tablegen (#200800)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit moves the non-VLX handling for VPMADD52 lowering out of X86ISelLowering.cpp and into TableGen patterns, and relaxes the C++ combine-side feature check so small v2i64/v4i64 PMADD52 combines are accepted with either IFMA or AVXIFMA. The visible lowering logic now relies on the new AVX512.td patterns to materialize 128/256-bit VPMADD52 via 512-bit forms when VLX is unavailable, and the tests were updated to expect zmm-based sequences plus kill annotations in NOVLX cases.
Changed symbols: matchVPMADD52; combineMulToPMADD52; X86InstrAVX512.td VPMADD52LUQ/VPMADD52HUQ patterns; slow-pmullq.ll; ifma-combine-vpmadd52.ll
Behavioral change: Removes an explicit C++ guard that rejected VPMADD52 matching for XMM/YMM sizes when AVX512VL was absent.; Changes combine eligibility from requiring IFMA+VLX or AVXIFMA to requiring IFMA or AVXIFMA for small vector widths.; Adds TableGen patterns that implement 128/256-bit PMADD52 via 512-bit instructions and subregister extraction when NoVLX is set.
Assertion or trace link: X86 DAG combine; SelectionDAG; X86ISelLowering.cpp; low bits constraint; peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc; combineBTToBitOpFlag
Reproducer link: Clang crashes at -O1 during X86 DAG instruction selection; reduced C testcase; backend assertion during combine/lowering
Pass or subsystem link: X86 instruction selection lowering; SelectionDAG combine; bit-test / PMADD52 lowering
Causal explanation: The commit is clearly in the X86 lowering/combine area and changes how small-vector PMADD52 is matched and legalized, which is adjacent to the reported crash subsystem. However, the retrieved hunks only show PMADD52 feature gating and pattern selection, not the specific low-bits constraint or bit-test combine logic named in the issue. So it is plausible as a backend-lowering risk factor, but the evidence does not directly connect it to the assertion 'low bits constraint must survive width adjustment'.
Causal confidence: 0.34
Build risk: Touches X86ISelLowering.cpp and X86InstrAVX512.td, both high-risk backend files; Changes codegen for NOVLX/AVX512 feature combinations; Updates codegen tests for both 128-bit and 256-bit PMADD52 lowering

+              (INSERT_SUBREG (v8i64 (IMPLICIT_DEF)), VR128X:$z, sub_xmm)), sub_xmm)>;
+
+  def : Pat<(v4i64 (x86vpmadd52l VR256X:$x, VR256X:$y, VR256X:$z)),
+            (EXTRACT_SUBREG

+              (INSERT_SUBREG (v8i64 (IMPLICIT_DEF)), VR256X:$y, sub_ymm),
+              (INSERT_SUBREG (v8i64 (IMPLICIT_DEF)), VR256X:$z, sub_ymm)), sub_ymm)>;
+  def : Pat<(v4i64 (x86vpmadd52l VR256X:$x, VR256X:$y, VR256X:$z)),

+              (INSERT_SUBREG (v8i64 (IMPLICIT_DEF)), VR256X:$x, sub_ymm),
+              (INSERT_SUBREG (v8i64 (IMPLICIT_DEF)), VR256X:$y, sub_ymm),
+              (INSERT_SUBREG (v8i64 (IMPLICIT_DEF)), VR256X:$z, sub_ymm)), sub_ymm)>;
+}

Summary: This commit adds an X86 SelectionDAG combine that fuses a BT with a sibling bit-modifying operation into a single flag-producing BTR/BTS/BTC node when both operations target the same bit. It introduces helper logic to peel through truncation, zero-extension, any-extension, and masking that preserves the low bit-index bits, plus new X86 SDNodes, instruction patterns, and regression tests.
Changed symbols: peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc; combineBTToBitOpFlag; combineBT; X86btr; X86bts; X86btc; X86ISelLowering.cpp; X86InstrFragments.td
Behavioral change: Adds a combine that recognizes BT plus a sibling AND/OR/XOR bit-modify on the same source and merges them into BTR/BTS/BTC while preserving CF semantics.; Introduces a width-aware helper that strips TRUNCATE/ZERO_EXTEND/ANY_EXTEND and AND masks only when the low log2(bitwidth) bits survive.; Asserts that BT bit indices are only formed for i32/i64 and that width adjustment must preserve the low-bit constraint.
Assertion or trace link: low bits constraint must survive width adjustment; peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc; combineBTToBitOpFlag; X86ISelLowering.cpp; SelectionDAG combine; bit-test lowering
Reproducer link: Clang crashes at -O1 during X86 DAG instruction selection; crash/assertion in X86 backend combine logic involving bit-test and width adjustment
Pass or subsystem link: X86 DAG combine; X86ISelLowering; SelectionDAG; bit-test lowering

top_candidates.subject: [SPIR-V] Select int-to-int convert opcode from source signedness (#201116)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes SPIR-V builtin conversion lowering so integer-to-integer convert opcodes are selected from the source operand's signedness rather than the destination's signedness. It also adds a SPIR-V codegen test covering signed/unsigned source and destination combinations for convert builtins.
Changed symbols: generateConvertInst; SPIRVBuiltins.cpp; ConvertBuiltin; convert_signedness.ll
Behavioral change: For integer convert builtins, choose OpSConvert vs OpUConvert based on whether the source type is signed.; Adjust builtin conversion lowering semantics for SPIR-V integer casts; no X86 DAG combine or bit-test lowering logic is touched.
Assertion or trace link: low bits constraint must survive width adjustment; peekThroughBitPosExtTrunc; combineBTToBitOpFlag; X86ISelLowering.cpp
Reproducer link: Clang crashes at -O1 during X86 DAG instruction selection; backend assertion in X86 SelectionDAG combine / bit-test lowering
Pass or subsystem link: SPIR-V builtin lowering; SPIR-V codegen
Causal explanation: The retrieved hunks only affect SPIR-V builtin conversion opcode selection and its tests. The reported bug is an X86 DAG combine assertion in X86ISelLowering.cpp involving bit-position width adjustment and bit-test lowering. There is no evidence in the visible patch that this commit changes X86 target lowering, SelectionDAG combines, or integer width/sign-extension reasoning relevant to the crash, so it is unlikely to be the cause or fix.
Causal confidence: 0.98
Build risk: Touches only SPIR-V backend code and SPIR-V tests; No overlap with X86 target lowering or SelectionDAG combine paths; Behavior is limited to integer convert opcode selection

selected_hunks.patch:
diff --git a/llvm/lib/Target/SPIRV/SPIRVBuiltins.cpp b/llvm/lib/Target/SPIRV/SPIRVBuiltins.cpp
index 9bc29dd0103a..3e0de48a8134 100644
--- a/llvm/lib/Target/SPIRV/SPIRVBuiltins.cpp
+++ b/llvm/lib/Target/SPIRV/SPIRVBuiltins.cpp
@@ -3211,0 +3212,2 @@ static bool generateConvertInst(const StringRef DemangledCall,
+    bool IsSourceSigned =
+        DemangledCall[DemangledCall.find_first_of('(') + 1] != 'u';

diff --git a/llvm/test/CodeGen/SPIRV/transcoding/OpenCL/convert_signedness.ll b/llvm/test/CodeGen/SPIRV/transcoding/OpenCL/convert_signedness.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..d20d6a1e7993
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/CodeGen/SPIRV/transcoding/OpenCL/convert_signedness.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+; Check that convert_ builtins pick the signed/unsigned opcode from the source
+; operand signedness.
+
+; RUN: llc -O0 -mtriple=spirv32-unknown-unknown %s -o - | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: %if spirv-tools %{ llc -O0 -mtriple=spirv32-unknown-unknown %s -o - -filetype=obj | spirv-val %}
+
+; CHECK-DAG: OpName %[[#StoS:]] "s_to_s"
+; CHECK-DAG: OpName %[[#StoU:]] "s_to_u"
+; CHECK-DAG: OpName %[[#UtoS:]] "u_to_s"
+; CHECK-DAG: OpName %[[#UtoU:]] "u_to_u"
+; CHECK-DAG: OpName %[[#StoF:]] "s_to_f"
+; CHECK-DAG: OpName %[[#UtoF:]] "u_to_f"
+
+; signed source -> signed dest: sign-extend.
+; CHECK: %[[#StoS]] = OpFunction
+; CHECK: OpSConvert
+define spir_func void @s_to_s(i32 noundef %x) {
+  call spir_func i64 @_Z12convert_longi(i32 noundef %x)
+  ret void
+}
+
+; signed source -> unsigned dest: sign-extend.
+; CHECK: %[[#StoU]] = OpFunction
+; CHECK: OpSConvert
+define spir_func void @s_to_u(i32 noundef %x) {
+  call spir_func i64 @_Z13convert_ulongi(i32 noundef %x)
+  ret void
+}
+
+; unsigned source -> signed dest: zero-extend.
+; CHECK: %[[#UtoS]] = OpFunction
+; CHECK: OpUConvert
+define spir_func void @u_to_s(i32 noundef %x) {
+  call spir_func i64 @_Z12convert_longj(i32 noundef %x)
+  ret void
+}
+
+; unsigned source -> unsigned dest: zero-extend.
+; CHECK: %[[#UtoU]] = OpFunction
+; CHECK: OpUConvert
+define spir_func void @u_to_u(i32 noundef %x) {
+  call spir_func i64 @_Z13convert_ulongj(i32 noundef %x)
+  ret void
+}
+
+; signed source -> float.
+; CHECK: %[[#StoF]] = OpFunction
+; CHECK: OpConvertSToF
+define spir_func void @s_to_f(i32 noundef %x) {
+  call spir_func float @_Z13convert_floati(i32 noundef %x)
+  ret void
+}
+
+; unsigned source -> float.
+; CHECK: %[[#UtoF]] = OpFunction
+; CHECK: OpConvertUToF
+define spir_func void @u_to_f(i32 noundef %x) {
+  call spir_func float @_Z13convert_floatj(i32 noundef %x)
+  ret void
+}
+
+declare spir_func i64 @_Z12convert_longi(i32 noundef)
+declare spir_func i64 @_Z13convert_ulongi(i32 noundef)
+declare spir_func i64 @_Z12convert_longj(i32 noundef)
+declare spir_func i64 @_Z13convert_ulongj(i32 noundef)
+declare spir_func float @_Z13convert_floati(i32 noundef)
+declare spir_func float @_Z13convert_floatj(i32 noundef)
